root_idea.summary: The root centers on being without covering or protection: nakedness, exposure, and open or unhidden space.
root_idea.development: The supplied lexical material extends this orientation from lack of clothing to exposed terrain, denuded objects, bareness of flesh, and related states of being unencumbered. Approach, release, and certain figurative uses are separately attested lexical branches rather than automatic meanings of every form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized noun citation form عَرَاءٌ.

senses.definition: To be or become naked, bare, or without clothing.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive state of lacking clothing; the lexical usage can also describe being bare of outer clothing while retaining one or more inner garments.

senses.definition: An open, exposed tract of land where nothing conceals or hides a person; an open shore or vacant surface.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the noun denotes an exposed place or shore, with the emphasis on its lack of shelter or concealment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become bare of flesh; to become lean.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied, for example, to a body that has become thin or fleshless.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become free from a fault, defect, blemish, or affair; to be exempt from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with مِنْ for release or exemption, including the conventional statement that no one is exempt from death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to or approach someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive usage synonymous with coming to or visiting someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To befall or afflict someone, especially with an evil or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the conventional expression اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء, ‘some of our gods has afflicted you with evil.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: To free someone from an affair or obligation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form II usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave something or let it alone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II usage applied broadly to an object or matter that is left unattended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ride horses without saddles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction describing riding unsaddled horses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To denude, strip, or make someone bare of clothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV construction used with the person and the garment or clothing removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pluck the hair from a horse’s tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive usage applied to a horse’s tail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey, remain, or dwell in a bare, open tract or in a lateral or adjacent area.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form IV usage associated with an exposed tract or its side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become distant, withdraw, or keep away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV usage expressing avoidance, remoteness, or withdrawal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ride a horse or other beast without a saddle or anything beneath the rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form XII construction; it can also describe venturing without protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To venture into a place of danger or difficulty without protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of riding or proceeding bare, including entering a waterless desert or places of peril without anything to shield one.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surmount or ride over hills or mounds, said of a mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage applied to a mirage overtopping elevated ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To undertake or commit an evil or foul thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form XII usage synonymous with doing or undertaking the act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey alone through the land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form XII usage emphasizing solitary travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard, elevated, or elevated-and-level open tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun has the plural أَعْرَاءٌ and is distinct in form from عَرَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wall, enclosed garden, or palm garden surrounded by a wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal usage equated with حائط and related enclosure terms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The condition of a horse being without a saddle, saddle-cloth, or other riding equipment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing an unsaddled horse or the state of riding without such equipment; it is not simply an adjective applied indiscriminately to a man or horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beautiful in the parts shown when unclad; beautiful in an unclad state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional descriptive expression, especially for a woman’s appearance when unclad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The exposed or visible parts of the body, especially the hands or arms, feet or legs, and face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer to parts that are normally visible or necessarily exposed; alternative reports extend it to places where the bones show and to the pudenda or vulva.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A naked, nude, bare, or unclothed person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The masculine form applies to a man and has a feminine counterpart عُرْيَانَةٌ; the word can also be extended to other things that are bare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An extended or gibbous tract of sand without trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use applied to a bare sandy tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Apparent or exposed, said of a plant or herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing vegetation that has become visible or exposed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wife; alternatively, one who does not conceal a secret.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional epithet whose interpretation is reported in these two related ways.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, active, quick, tall, and long-legged, said of a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative horse description, distinct from the literal sense of being unsaddled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nakedness or bareness of the bones through loss of flesh; leanness of the bones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression عَرَاءُ العِظَامِ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having little or no flesh on the two breasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Manifest or plainly evident, literally ‘naked’ of concealment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figuratively applied to truth or another matter that is exposed and clear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rugged road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported nominal usage with an uncertain transmitted spelling or morphological analysis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Places that do not produce plants or herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural nominal usage for barren or unproductive places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beds or bedding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate plural usage equated with فُرُشٌ; the form مَعَارِي may occur by poetic license.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel or other beast left to pasture by itself and carrying no burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized passive participle describing an unburdened, freely pastured animal.

cautions: The nominal Quran surface form عَرَاءِ is presented under the normalized dictionary citation form عَرَاءٌ.
The reported spelling and analysis of اِعْرَوْرَى in the rugged-road entry are uncertain, so that usage is retained with an explicit qualification.
No Maqāyīs entry was supplied; the root idea is therefore an orientation drawn from the supplied lexical material, not an independently sourced Maqāyīs formulation.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Mufradat row 967 also discusses عُرْوَةٌ, the tree called عُرْوَةٌ, and the legal-commercial term العَرَايَا. Those branches are not assigned here because their connection to the canonical QAC root عري is not independently established by the supplied Lane primary evidence.
